reviews.title: I highly recommend--especially for the older exerciser.
reviews.text:
First, I have to admit that I am not one of those people who loves to exercise. Any excuse will do to get me out of it. One of my most useful has been that hard surfaces hurt an old injury in my tailbone. Neither the bath mats I used at first, nor the thin and useless exercise mat I got later helped to make me feel either comfortable or secure.

This mat fortunately (or unfortunately, depending on how you look at it) removes that particular excuse. First, it is at least twice (probably even more than three times) as thick as the previous one I had. Secondly, the non-slip surface has a raised surface, a hill-and-valley design, that creates insulating air pockets that I appreciate, even on my unforgivingly hard tile or marble floors. (Supposedly, it's 3/8th of an inch, but I measure 1/2 inch on the "hill" parts). I'm not saying it's soft--it's not, I'm still exercising on a firm surface, but there is a significant difference when I'm flat on the floor whether I'm on my back, sides, on my knees, or upright. I don't feel the need to put a towel over it, like I did with my other mat, when lying down, and I feel very stable and secure when standing. I feel firmly grounded and don't constantly reach for something to hold on to.

Due to my age, I don't do anything very strenuous, I just work on flexibility and stability, I do exercises with small weights, repetitive joint strengthening exercises, and a lot of stretching and reaching. I've never done anything on this mat that involves jumping or using weights heavier than 5 lbs each, but the build and integrity of the mat suggests to me that it would hold up under much more intense conditions than those I subject it to. It also cleans very easily and I expect that it will be very durable.

The only problem I can see--and it doesn't affect me because I only use it at home--is rolling it back up to the size it originally came in, which is how it will fit back into the elastic carrier. If you're going to be taking it places, I hope you're much more coordinated than I am. (Actually, that isn't hard.)

reviews.title: Very thick, stays put on slick floors
reviews.text: This mat appears to actually be two different mats sealed together. The bottom one is black and ridged for traction against the floor. UPDATE 9/28/15 (Yes, I am still using this product):

This is for those looking for a mat that is not a yoga mat, this is not a yoga mat and is a lot thicker than a yoga mat, it is a thick corrugated exercise mat.

I have used this mat for just about every kind of stretched or strength training exercises. I mainly do martial arts and dance, and you do pretty intensive stretching and resistance exercises using your own body weight, for both. ORIGINAL REVIEW originally from 2011:

Had a few exercise and/or yoga mats, and a lot of times they aren't much better than exercising on the floor. This one is very thick and it is soft while still firm, but not obnoxiously thick, the bottom is ribbed, so I think that helps it feel thicker without being extremely thick, it helps the impact of your body be cushioned it seems. Done various exercises on it, stretches, pilates, and some of my custom exercises, and it didn't hurt my hip like it normally would on a hard surface or even sometimes on a carpet, so that is nice. The carrying strap is a nice additions well as none of my other mats have even had that, makes it a lot more convenient to carry around. :D

God Bless ~Amy

reviews.title: Great at First, But Not Durable Enough for Regular Use
reviews.text:
I really loved this mat at first. Yes, it was a little slick and smelly, as most new mats are, but after scrubbing with vinegar solution and letting it sit for a few days, the smell and residue were gone. The mat is soft and supportive, a good size for a taller person (I'm 5'11"), and non-toxic. The only drawback was that it was always kind of slick if my hands were sweaty (a problem in an 85 degree ashtanga studio - I can't even imagine doing hot yoga on this).

But after a few months, it began to shred where my feet are in a downward dog. It's been about 5 or 6 months of 3-5 practices a week, and dime-sized chunks are now missing. I leave class with blue plastic lint all over my pants and under my toenails (which I keep trimmed, thankyouverymuch).

In short, if you're doing a more relaxed style of yoga on a hard wood floor, this might be a nice cushy mat for you; it certainly feels great for savasana. But it is not durable under regular use, and it is not appropriate for a sweaty class.

reviews.title: excellent alternative to plastic
reviews.text:
i needed to replace my old yoga mat, which rats ate holes in when it was stored in the garage... i trimmed the eaten bits, but was left with something a bit too short for my workout, though good size for the beach!

i wanted to get a replacement mat that was not made from plastic, but options were limited. cork was interesting, but still backed with plastic...

i found this mat and decided to give it a shot. after my first workout on it, i am very pleased with my purchase so far!

what i like: 100% cotton, thick sturdy weave (similar to my rug under it actually!), feels durable, bright colors, stays put while i move, grippy texture.

what i don't like: smells a little musty (but i'm sure that'll air out if i put it in the sun for a couple hours), a little rough on the hands (just not as plush as plastic mats, but it's fine), and lastly unsure what the coating on the base is (the coating under the mat is very effective at keeping the mat in place while you workout, on carpet or on the hard floor, but i wish i knew what it was.. is it plastic? glue? it's got an almost waxy texture, i hope it's natural and not micro plastics but i'm not certain - any info from the manufacturer would be great!)

anyway i think this is an awesome mat for someone that wants to avoid plastic, it looks great and always nice to be a little more earth friendly. it's not as soft as foam mats, but it's fine (esp if you are using it on carpet).

reviews.title: Nice mat- read below to be sure it will fit your sizing needs..!!!
reviews.text:
This mat is nice quality for the price.. it would be great for any beginner for sure! The length is where you need to be sure you get the right/good fit- and this mat is 6 feet long. This may seem plenty big, especially for someone like me as, I’m 5’1”..!! However, keep in mind… Is the movement and stretches you’ll be doing while on your mat! And for those much taller then, my 5ft self- this may pose a bit of a problem by not providing enough length..
•Best way to avoid getting a mat that is too short-
is to raise arms to a relaxed stance above head.. then, add that measurement to your total height- (from top if head to end of palms- add on these inches- not entire arms length!!) this will insure you’ll fit on your mat during all sun salutations and downward dogs! Makes sense.. But, something I hadn’t realized when ordering. Even so, @ 5ft. tall and reach of my arm still left me approx 4+” to spare- But, something to definitely be aware of when selecting!
•Strap is easy to put on and is all one piece-
Assemble in elastic material and has reinforced stitching to avoid breaking. **dont throw it away!! The strap was loose in bottom of box- and if you don’t look thoroughly, it could easily make it out to the trash- mine did!! But, once I realize it was missing I retraced my steps and found it on the bottom of the tubed boxed! Just pat attn.- this IS NOT placed on mat when it arrives!!! **Bonus: I LOVE the length of the strap.. not too long to bounce around your knees and get in the way when carried- This strap offers just enough slack to carry of the shoulder perfectly- I attached photos.. and this is perfect length!!! (length is NOT adjustable!)

•Not all mats are created equal! BUT.. A thinner mat is not always a bad thing. I did order one with extra thickness before.. tbh, it’s very “grabby” on the feet.. This is thinner so, yes! You may feel pressure points on the floor a bit more however, this mat allows for easy movement with the feet- I loved the textured surface- it helps keeps feet from becoming sweaty and slipping!
• I have used the mat a handful of times.. and maybe OCD about disinfecting after every use, I don’t care! I use a misting mat cleaner that is all natural.. I spray both sides with a light coat. So far, we’ve held up just fine! No sticky or, peeling of the mat itself- **the key here people: to let cleaner dry before rolling/storing your mat!!! Here’s a Life hack: whenever you clean your mat, always be sure it’s 100% dry before rolling/storing! You will thank me for this and mats life expectancy will last much longer than you think! Not too mention, you won’t be the one who’s mat stinks up the room for the whole class.. that’s always a good thing!!
Overall, this is a great mat and good investment for any who need a clean, nice, decent space to do their exercises- it may not have all the added extras but, for many... those are just that, extra!
I can recommend this feeling confident it can do it’s job and one will get their moneys worth.
I hope this info helps.. feel free to let me know!

reviews.title: Love this mat so much that I just ordered another one.
reviews.text:
After 2 and a half years of fairly heavy use, I decided it was finally time to replace this mat. And the main reason for replacing it was because one of my cats decided to start scratching up the surface - my bad for letting it sit where she could reach it. I debated getting a different mat to replace it - manduka, jade, lulu? I read reviews. I talked to other yogis. And I decided to stick with what I already know I like and ordered another gaiam dry-grip. It's worked great in any type of class I've tried. Never had any issues with slipping. And I like the subtle design - not as boring as a plain colored mat, but not in your face either. I like that there's a little bit of extra weight to it - it stays in place on the studio floor and no worries about wind during outdoor classes. If I had to name a draw back, it would be that it is not reversible.

Original Review:
I have owned the black version of this mat for over a year and a half and it is still going strong. I'm so use to it that I have a hard time using the normal studio mats anymore on the rare occasion that I forget it. The mat still looks great and I still get people telling me that they like my mat and asking me what it is. I like that it has a design on it, but that it's subtle and not so in your face as a lot of mats. I take 3-4 yoga classes a week in addition to a home practice. This mat works great for flow, hot, aerial - basically any class I've used it in. I've even used it for some outdoor classes. I am not a heavy sweater, but in hot classes when I do work up a sweat, I've never had issues with slipping. The grip is great and the mat provides a good cushion over hard floors. Other mats I tried seemed squishy and the thickness just condensed down to nothing, but this mat is nice and dense and sturdy. To clean it, I just toss it in my bathtub and just use water to wipe it down super good and then let it air dry.

reviews.title: Perfect for aerobics or for using under a step
reviews.text:
I was looking for a yoga mat that was thin enough to be stable under an aerobics step yet firm enough with enough give to use for shock absorption when dancing or running in place. I wasn't expecting miracles, but after reading many, many reviews, I decided to for for this one based on thinness, price, reviews of this mat and others and - what the heck - I liked the color. The one I ordered is the Turquoise Sea 4mm mat, and I paid full price for it out of my own pocket.

I was expecting to have to put the mat open in the garage for a few days, but when I pulled it out of the box and the plastic bag, it had no smell whatever. It is, indeed, quite thin - I prefer a thicker mat for poses on my knees or for doing situps on, but it's perfect for my needs. It keeps my aerobic step in place like it's glued to the floor, and it's actually really good at absorbing some of the impact when I walk or dance on it. Oh, and the color is exactly the same as it appeared on my monitor.

I expected to have to buy several mats before I found the right one, but I got lucky with this mat. I've bought a lot of things on Amazon that are okay, but for one reason or another, they are pretty meh. This mat isn't one of them. It is exactly what I wanted it to be with no smells and an attractive color. It is, indeed, sticky on the floor, and while it's too soon to see how durable it will be, it doesn't shed. And it's thin. It probably won't be enough padding if you want to spend long periods of time on your knees or doing 100 situps, but if you're actually looking for a thin mat, this 4mm one is definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: A good yoga mat for the money!
reviews.text:
I have included a picture of the mat with a Sprite bottle for color reference.

Yes, the color of the dark green mat in person looks different than shown online. The green is that cool pine forest tree muted greyed green color and not a bright green color.

The mat also comes with some type of sparkle that does not rub off onto other surfaces.

The mat has a floral scent. I am not sure if this is the actual scent of the mat, or some type of coating applied to it, but I find it pleasant. That may not be the case for everyone and there are people with scent sensitivities that may not find that appealing to them.

The textured alignment lines are an excellent feature and one of my main reasons for purchasing this mat. You can definitely feel them without looking, which is exact what I was looking for in a yoga mat.

I am using this mat on old painted wood floor and it does not slip.

The mat came with a strap for neatly tucking it away on my wall rack.

Overall, for less than $25, this yoga mat can not be beat and has a lot going for it.

Over time, I will update this review with details on durability.

As it stands, this yoga mat comes highly recommended!

reviews.title: Not padded, but definitely non-slipping
reviews.text:
The mat is described as being 1.5mm thick and I guess I hadn't thought that through fully. It is very thin, but definitely better than working out on a dirty floor. Once in place on my tile floor, it does not move, so the non-slip feature works well. It looks nice and provides for a clean surface to work on. The description says it is lightweight, but I'm not sure that I'd describe it that way. It's almost 3 lbs, but it does rollup into a very small package (remember, there is almost no padding). Perhaps, by lightweight, they mean that it isn't very thick? I also don't understand their reference to 'suede' in the description -- it is rubber through and through. Maybe they meant to describe it as 'suede-like' because that could make some sense -- the surface is soft and sort-of suede-like.

The material feels quite rugged and I think it'll last a long time. Once unrolled flat, it stays, and when rolled up, it maintains that shape, too. It is so very non-slip that if it is rolled and the edges aren't aligned, there is no fixing it -- usually, if the edges aren't aligned, I could tap on the edge sticking out and it would even up, but this one just stays uneven. This is not at all a problem, but if you like your roll to be even, you'll have to be careful to align the edge with each roll.

I received mine about a week ago, and it has become my go-to mat. I am airline crew, so I initially purchased this for travel, but because i live in a downtown city area, this is much better for carrying between classes, coffee shops, hanging out, and doing other things than a traditional rolled mat. It is lightweight, easy to fold, sturdy, grippy, and the integrated straps are perfect.

My only small complaint is the smell. It does have a strong smell of rubber, and it leaves a weird smell on my hands after I wash it. Hopefully that will dissipate with use and regular cleaning.

UPDATE: So after using this almost daily for a little over a week, I have to say I’m not as impressed with the grip. If you use it in a cooler room and your hands and feet stay perfectly dry during your practice, the grip is perfect. But if you sweat at all like I do, even during a regular practice, any moisture at all makes it very slippery. Even my rubber-lined towel slides off of it during hot yoga. Also, I’ve washed it in my washer and let it hang dry for several days, and the smell of rubber is still present. I only removed one star though, because the portable design and the sustainable rubber are high priorities, I just need a grippier towel.

reviews.title: Great for home practice but do not roll it up!
reviews.text:
I have recently rediscovered my love of yoga and I had been looking for the perfect mat to do anywhere from 3.5 hours to 10+ hours of practice per week.

After doing hours upon hours of research, I decided to try a BMAT out. First of all, it is incredibly comfortable. Sure, it attracts hair/fur and smells like all rubber mats, but it is easy to wipe off with a damp microfiber cloth and it in no way smells toxic. I mainly leave it out in my home office/gym room and ensure it is away from sunlight, but I tried rolling it up once for a few minutes while vacuuming and regret it. There are now creases on the bottom facing part of the mat, and I would have expected better for the price. Lesson learned - I now hang it over furniture and make sure there are no folds on the mat. Regardless, I would recommend it for home practice for those who want something out of rubber and don't expect 10 years out of a rubber mat (check out other big name brands, rubber mats just fall apart over time). I look forward to at least a year of yoga on this mat, 18 months if I am lucky! This mat would cost around 25 cents per day if it lasts a year - which I think is still a good value.

reviews.title: Good quality, attractive yoga mat
reviews.text:
This mat is sold specifically for yoga, but there are multiple possibilities for its use. It is also excellent for other types of exercise such as resistance-band exercises, Pilates, and various types of core work and stretching. It can be used as a camping mat, too.

I got this mat in the "blue shadow" shade. It is a lovely, light-green color. This mat is 68 inches long, which is a similar length to a regular mattress. Like most yoga mats, it has a soft, spongy, comfortable feel. It has a bumpy, sticky texture to prevent slipping. The instructions from the manufacturer are to wipe it down with a damp cloth just before using it to further increase the stickiness. It is also easy to keep this mat clean by wiping it down regularly with a damp, soft cloth.

I own four different brands of yoga mats, and several of the mats I own are of this same Gaiam brand. It's a bit more expensive than the generic brands sold at big-box, discount stores, but it seems to be worth the extra money. Especially since, as advertised, it does not seem to have as much of a toxic smell as most yoga mats do.

This is a 5 mm thick mat, and it might not be quite thick enough for some people. Yoga mats come in various thicknesses, however, so it is possible to get a thicker mat from this same Gaiam brand if desired. If you are working out on hard concrete or ceramic-tile flooring, a 5 mm mat like this one might not be enough padding. You might want a 10 mm mat instead.

reviews.title: Grippy and cushy
reviews.text:
This Gaiam mat is good for people with sweaty hands and feet like myself, or people who do hot yoga. I sweat so much due to medical issues I have to use yoga towels, yoga socks, and bear paw hand grips...so I was very interested in trying a mat that touts grippy benefits. It's no fun doing yoga when half of your focus is on not sliding off the mat.

This 5mm mat offers generous padding and doesn't slide around on the floor. It helps with grip when you get it, especially if you damped it slightly before using to activate what makes it kind of "tacky". It's not sticky or anything, it just helps.

It's also made with less controversial materials than other mats so if that's a concern this is a good option. It is free of DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DIDP, and DNOP phthalates.

reviews.text: I ordered this this Yoga Starter Set because I seem to have lost my yoga items when I moved across the country to a new state. This set would suit my needs as I wanted to get involved with yoga classes again.  I like the fact that the backpack is made of water-resistant material and the zippers are constructed in a way to resist water going into the backpack if worn in the rain.  My concern with this backpack is that the material used is thin and prone to damage from sharp objects. When I opened this backpack, I noticed there was section reserved for a small laptop or tablet in the main compartment in the back.  There are 2 zipped pockets in the front and one in the back, as well as 2 side slip pockets to fit an umbrella or thin water bottle.  The front main compartment contained all the Yoga materials (a folded yoga mat, 2 cork blocks, 1 strap) and a thin zipped polyester bag that seemed to be reserved for shoes or wet clothing.  Unfortunately, this bag is unlined so I would have to put my shoes or wet clothing in a plastic bag first before using this extra bag. The yoga blocks made of cork are heavy and good quality. Yoga mat is the standard size (72 inches long 24 inches wide) and I really like the fact that it is 5 mm thick since I wanted a good cushion on the floor.  The yoga strap is OK.  It is thinner than what I am used to. Overall, I find the items pretty good for a yoga beginner and recommend to anyone who wants to get started.

reviews.title: Great mat, very impressed with it.
reviews.text:
This seems like an excellent, well made yoga mat. Having only used it a few times it's a little tough give firm opinions on it as some of the things could go either way over the long haul. However, I like it a lot and it's currently my main mat. Here's what I've found so far:

Pros:
Better than average grip, almost too good. It can be hard to make slight adjustments, requiring you to pick up your hand/foot instead of just slide it slightly. A little annoying for transitions like Warrior 1 to Warrior 2. However, overall it's a good feature. It's still slippery when wet. So in a hot class the grip might last a little longer, but as soon as there's significant sweat, you're going to need a towel.

Good materials and construction. The bottom has a different texture than the top. They say you can use either side, but it seems like the lighter side texture is better for gripping the floor. So far I've only used it with the darker side facing up.

The mat is very thick and feels like felt. Personally, I like mats on the thicker side so I think it's great. The 'felt' feel to it worries me a little bit since it seems like it'll absorb sweat and require more cleaning than usual. So far no problem, but we'll see.

It's a bit too thick/soft to use on carpet. It's great on a hardwood floor, so when I'm in a studio it's fine. However, I occasionally practice at my house and it has carpet. A thinner mat works better for that. Not really a complaint, just a fyi, the ProSource mat is clearly designed for use on a hard floor and it works great there.

Long: 72" A requirement for me since I'm 6 feet tall.

Cons:

I'm getting used to the extra grip. As mentioned, it makes slight adjustments a bit more difficult.

It feels kind of plush. I like thick mats, so it's great, but it may not be for everyone.

The claim of TPE being 'environmentally friendly' is a bit of stretch. It's better than PVC but there seems to be mixed information about how eco-friendly it is. And trying to find a place to recycle a TPE mat is difficult. you can't just put it in the recycle bin. Something to consider if you _really_ want a eco-mat.

reviews.title: I'm so disappointed...
reviews.text:
I really really wanted to like this. There were tons of rave reviews all over the internet for this mat. In particular, countless mentions of how unbelievably sticky it is. Basically endless claims of how it's the stickiest mat they've ever felt.

I hardly ever sweat at all on my body. I am not a sweaty person. However, my hands and feet? They can get pretty wet. That being said, it's incredibly important for me to use a sticky mat to maintain Downdog and other asanas.

When I first excitedly ripped open the packaging on this mat, I was immediately smacked in the face with this incredibly strong odor.
"What IS that?!" I exclaimed.
"It smells like...fish." my mom replied while wrinkling her nose.

AND IT DOES. IT REEKED OF FISH. Those complaints about the Jade Harmony mat and the Lululemon mats smelling bad? They ain't got nothin' on this Eau de Fish. Luckily, after unrolling it on the floor and leaving it to air out overnight, the odor dissipated. So I was able to take the mat to class without smelling like a seafood market.

The surface of this mat is quite smooth, unlike the rough texture of the Jade Harmony. Though not as smooth as the smooth side of a Lululemon mat. When your hands are dry, without a doubt, the grip on this Bmat is quite good. My mother said it was much too grippy for her tastes.

I took my Bmat to an easygoing Hatha yoga class this morning and lemme tell ya. It was like a SLIP 'N SlIDE. As soon as my hands had a hint of sweat on them, they started slipping. The worst part was, when my feet started sweating as well, the sweat began to literally pool on top of the smooth mat into little mini puddles. I'm not even the type of person that drips sweat. It was purely sweat from my hands and feet. And because of the smooth surface, there was no place for the water to go. It just sat there.
I could barely even hold an asana as upright as a Warrior 2 because of how dang slippery this mat was.

Even my mom's $10 generic yoga mat that I've been using for the past few weeks felt better than this $85 (including tax) designer mat. The generic yoga mat has that rounded bumps texture that I could at least hold on to if I was sweaty. Because the Bmat is smooth, when I was sweaty, I had absolutely nothing to grip on to so I was constantly slipping.
I spent the whole class feeling so unstable I couldn't enjoy my hour of yoga practice whatsoever.

Pros:
- Made in Spain
- Pretty color
- Seems like a good company

Cons:
- Out of the box has a strong fishy smell
- Pools sweat
- Super slippery with even a hint of wetness

Even when dry, this mat is not as grippy as a Lululemon mat. I know a lot of people crap on that mat (maybe because they think the company is so overrated?) but I really think it's quite good. I loved the Jade Harmony's stickiness as well (it even ripped a couple of my hairs out on occasion), but the smell was pretty overwhelming and never really went away. It's also super heavy.

Anyway, I'm really sorry this mat didn't work out for me. I was really looking forward for this to be a winner after all the good reviews. But like all things, your mileage may vary and you don't know until you try it yourself. Back to Amazon it goes!

Hauls a lot of gear in a a sturdy cotton canvas pack. Water proofed with oilcloth treatment and it's good to go anywhere you want it. The metal tabs on the end of the straps are merely compression for from factory so the do pop off on their own after a while. So I jumped on it while I was waterproofing the bag, popped them off and refit them with epoxy glue and compression fit, so they wont budge now.

reviews.title: Above average minimalist no frills pack with some minor gripes.
reviews.text: I'm a minimalist, I count my weight in ozs, and have been backpacking for 24 years. Gear has changed a lot through the years, and I've been through my share of packs. For a an average 6 day trip my pack will weigh between 17-25 lbs depending on the season. This includes my shelter, sleep system, cooking, fuel, food, 4lbs of water and everything I need to survive. This isn't my lightest pack. What caught my attention were the load lifters, which really do help duffle bag style packs ride a little better. Overall I was satisfied with this pack. It had a ton of room, I didn't use a pack cover I use compactor bags and atuff sacks to keep my gear dry. So far no leaks no problems. I'm not gentle with my gear and so far despite putting hundreds of miles on this pack no issues. I wish the mesh pouch on the front was a tad bigger I leave my 19 oz tarp tent and 2 oz ground cover in it to dry along with a few things however it does take some working packing them in to the mesh. The side pockets are deep and snug. I don't like that there aren't any hip belt pockets. I bought some cubein fiber ones from zpaks which fit okay...  I don't like the way the belt is attached to the buckle I have a lot of extra material dangling from both sides. Other than those few gripes the pack has performed well, and has been comfortable. I felt like I got a good deal with the price being so low.

reviews.title: Good enough for occasional day-hikes , has a carbon fiber external frame/brace , fairly lightweight
reviews.text:
I've used the Kailas Wind Tunnel backpack on a couple short hikes around Prescott, AZ and Camp Verde. So far I haven't experienced any issues with it even though I haven't been gentle with it (tossed it onto the ground/rocks a few times, scuffed some tree branches). The seams are holding and the nylon hasn't ripped even when packed with about 10-15lbs worth of gear.

Design wise it's similar to some of the other entry level daypacks from name brand outfitters. I was surprised to see a carbon reinforcement frame on the back. I was worried it may dig into my back when hiking but so far it hasn't. I like the ergonomics of it as well but I haven't gone on any longer day-hikes yet so I'll update this review if I end up disliking it.

reviews.title: Pretty solid short hiking bag!
reviews.text: This Kailas bag is really quite nice. It has a lightweight internal frame to give your back a little separation and ventilation. Overall all of the seams are stitched well and it presents as a pretty decent quality pack. I'd compare it to an REI Co-Op branded bag in the same general price category. Time will tell how it holds up, but so far it looks like it should be a relatively durable bag. There is not a ton of padding in the straps, but it is intended to be a lightweight bag. The included rain cover in the bottom of the pack is a nice addition. The blue fabric is a good color and the pack overall looks pretty modern and trendy. Kailas is a brand worth keeping an eye on, it seems like some of their other offerings are fairly solid as well. Decent quality pack and overall decent buy, especially if you don't have a nearby outdoor store to try stuff locally.

reviews.title: Very Comfortable Backpack!
reviews.text: This is my favorite backpack for hiking! It fits really well, and it has an amazing number of expandable pockets also.  I like the space suspension feature for your back. This will keep the backpack cool while hiking in hot weather. One surprise I wasn’t expecting was the rain cover that you can find in the bottom zippered compartment. Now your backpack can be protected rain or shine. It is a little heavier than I expected. But not so much that it would be too heavy with my using it on hikes through the preserves here in Southwest Florida.  It has loads of room in the inner compartment. The padded shoulder straps adjust perfectly for me, I’m 5’9”, and it feels very comfortable.  I highly recommend this backpack.

reviews.title: Little pricey, but pretty good pack
reviews.text:
I picked up this bag awhile back and I am generally pleased with it. The 28L capacity is suitable for a weekend camping trip, and the included rain cover is a useful feature for unexpected weather. The backpack seems well-constructed with solid zippers and comfortable straps.

The only minor issue I have is with the price, which I think is a bit steep at $70. However, the backpack's quality and added features do justify the cost to some extent.

Overall, I would rate this backpack 3.5 out of 5 stars. I would recommend it to someone looking for a spacious and dependable camping backpack, but be aware of the slightly higher price tag.

reviews.title: Total Osprey dupe!
reviews.text: This hiking pack is amazing! The quality is top-notch. If you are familiar with Osprey backpacks, this feels like a total dupe. The features, design, materials, quality, zippers, and accessories all feel identical to a hiking pack priced at least $100 more at REI. The outlet for a hydration pack hose was a little tricky to find, but it's just the half-moon slit at the top right where it makes sense for it to be.  I seriously can't enough wonderful things, it's just SO nice. This would make a fantastic gift for anyone that hikes.

reviews.title: Superb Value Disc Bag
reviews.text:
I bought this for 60 bucks. At that price point you are getting an insanely good value. I upgraded from DD Trooper which is similar and did an admirable job for a couple of years but did finally start to wear out. I was going to spend a bit more ($100 range) for an upgraded bag, but after seeing this one I realized that I could get all the features I wanted for less. Now I do have friends that have more expensive bags from US manufacturers and I won't knock them at all. They seem very happy with those bags but the cost ramps up into the $300 + range, which was simply more than I was willing to spend.

So what you get in the paratrooper is a sturdy and functional bag. The main pouch can easily hold up to 20 discs. I probably would suggest holding a couple less in there as if you use the putter pouch it restricts the ease of access to the main pouch. By leaving a little room in there you can more easily insert and remove discs you use. The paratrooper comes with two compartments above the main opening, and I use them both. One I use for putters and the other I use for my go to mid range and second most used driver. Then on the flap for the main pouch I use my go to driver. So I have 6 discs that are very easily accessible, which is awesome because those are truly the ones I use the most.

For the side pouches, they are large and plenty big to store whatever I need on the course. I have sunblock, bug spray, extra towel, sharpie and I keep my phone, keys and wallet in my bag while I play. They also have an interior pocked for sliding in your phone or wallet. Very nice. I like having two water bottle holders. One I use with a 40 oz bottle and it easily fits. The other I tuck in a towel and grip sack. This allows me to keep those things dry on damp days. On hotter days or multi-round days, I would imagine I would bring 2 water bottles unless I knew of a place to refill my 40 oz bottle.

The bag comes with 4 plastic inserts (1 for each side) to keep the bag stable. I think you can decide whether or not to use them. I tried them with and without and have decided that I prefer the extra stability that they offer. It is slightly softer and probably more comfortable bag to carry with them out, but I would frankly rather have the bag be more rigid. I noticed that the bag tended to fall over more without the inserts. The one insert I decided to leave out was the front one, as I wanted the front of the bag to be more pliable for easy disc removal. The zippers are elastic bands which are nice as they are easy to grab and you can clip things through the loops.

Cons. No bag is perfect so the small nit picky things I would point out is that it would be nice to have a couple of d-rings at the top of the bag as the trooper had to clip on things like towels or dry sacks. But as noted before there are other places to stick those things. Also you can buy a small carabiner and attach it to the zipper for the top putter pouch. The top easy access pouch is a little big and when used can interfere a bit with the accessibility of discs in the main pouch. I took a couple of safety pins to make the very top pouch slightly less deep and the second pouch I used the velcro to pin it to the back of the bag.

In sum, you get a ton of features for the price paid. I have seen plenty of bags at twice the price with similar or less features. I can't fully speak to the durability, as I have only used it for a couple of weeks, but my impression is that it is well made and I expect it to last several years. I highly recommend this bag. I don't think you will be disappointed if you give it a try.

reviews.title: IN DEPTH Review Of This Backpack
reviews.text:
WARNING- This is an IN DEPTH review of this backpack to help those who are trying to make serious buying decisions. If you prefer a more brief summary, please see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
----------------------------
When it comes to summer time and even Spring or Fall, my family loves to go for hikes. Sometimes it involves overnights. The talk of the family has been to want to bring a backpack along with tent and sleeping arrangements on an overnight hike in some great land around some lakes. I knew that our usual backpacks would not suffice, so when I saw this, I thought it would be perfect. Let's see how this measures up to what we need.

WHAT IS THIS BACKPACK LIKE?
The backpack has a very thick woven black fabric that is more like what you would find in a heavy jacket. It is not thin nylon that is sometimes found in backpacks. The black fabric is rugged. There is a sizeable gusset (10 inches) in the bottom which can be retracted with adjustable straps. These straps can hold a bedroll, small personal tent, or other similar things. The straps are pretty long so I am thinking the capacity is quite adaptable. That means you can pack a small personal tent AND bedroll or portable small cot (we have one that would fit perfectly here).

SIDE POCKETS
There are two small net pockets which can hold water bottles or similar things, and also side long zipped pockets which have cords on them for easy quick access. The zipped pockets are angled, but they measure 9 inches tall at widest point. The highest point is 10 inches.

ADJUSTABLE STRAPS
There are quite a few pair of adjustable straps:
- under backpack
-upper sides
-small circular straps at upper edge of back pocket
-from backpack to top of shoulder straps on the front (possibly can hold small roll of some sort)
-center of each shoulder strap to hook and hold backpack in place
-on padded waist belt to hold in place
-at base of padded waist belt to hold backpack to waistband for security
-in between shoulder straps in loop form to hang backpack from

BACK CENTER COMPARTMENT
This pocket has a tough handle on it so that you can lift the pack out when it is zipped. Inside there are three pocket compartments- two netted and one nylon. Compartment is 11 inches high, and pockets are- nylon: 7 1/2 high and nylon are 6 inches high and 5 inches wide each. The compartment itself is a little over 10 inches wide. The entire compartment has a double two way zipper which means that you can open it down each side or the entire way by sliding both heads to one side.

TOP BACK COMPARTMENT
This compartment is at the top of the back. It is about 9 x 9 approximately. This pocket has a place with a strap and a plastic/nylon hook so you can hang keys from it if you need to. The gusseting in the pocket allows bulky items to be put in this pocket. It is not too deep or too shallow to be practical.

PADDING AND SHOULDER STRAPS/HARNESS
The padding on this is great. The back itself is reinforced and very stiff, yet comfortable. It has plenty of padding on it for comfort while walking with a loaded pack. The straps have great padding on them as well. There is plenty of padding on the waist belt as well, with extra padding on the small of the back for comfort and ease of walking with support.

MAIN COMPARTMENT
This compartment is very deep and only has an elasticized pleated pocket in it which is on the reinforced back panel (the one that goes on your back when wearing the backpack). The entire compartment is approimately 22 inches in depth. The elasticized pocket inside is about 10 inches high. Width of back panel is about 12 inches. The compartment can extend up to 12 inches out if packed fully. There is another hook in this compartment to hang keys from etc.

WATER BAG
If you want to carry a water bag in the backpack, it would fit in here, and there is a little hole that you can slip the tube through for drinking. We do not use a water bag at this point so I can not comment on the usefulness of this feature.

WORKMANSHIP
This backpack seems to be made in top quality workmanship. The sewing is great, no loose threads, and all of the bindings and zippers seem to be in very well with no gaps or missed stitches.

OUR EXPERIENCE WITH THIS BACKPACK
So far, we have just had all day hikes with this- no bedroll or personal tent yet as it has been way too snowy and cold so far. However, as a backpack in general, we have packed this thing up well. I also did take it to a large fiber festival which required me to slip things rolled up into the straps and also to pack the backpack pretty well. It was easy to walk in and comfortable as well. I spent almost an entire day with it and it did not make me all stiff at the end of the day like some packs will do.

UPDATES
I will be updating this as we have a chance to use it over the summer for camping and serious overnight hiking as well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Made with excellent workmanship, tough fabric, and well thought out, this backpack is great for hiking, even if a personal tent and/or bedroll or cot is desired to carry with you on a trek. Use of water pack is possible with this backpack although we have not used it in that capacity as of yet. The padding is comfortable and supportive and the backpack itself is easy to pack and carry if you are careful how you set it up for most balance and comfort as with any backpack.

MY RATING
This is five stars. It seems like it will meet our needs perfectly and I will update when I have more experiences to add to this review if applicable.

reviews.title: Above Average Backpack
reviews.text:
This is a good quality backpack that seems to be most useful for hiking and casual comping trips. At its current price, it is an excellent value for the money. All of the basics of a quality hiking pack are there with more than enough pockets and compartments for most and a cavernous main body that could probably hold most of the clothes I own in it. Because of it's huge size, I would not recommend it for urban use or to simply carry things around town. While it is definitely comfortable enough for such use, it is pretty cumbersome to carry around with you when it's empty and definitely isn't something you would want to wear while on a bike or climbing on and off a bus.

The material is of well above average quality. It definitely is not waterproof, but it is at least water resistant. The padded straps are extremely comfortable to use, even when carrying heavy loads. If there is any weak link in the construction, it would probably be in the stitching. The thread is fairly thick, but there are no double stitched areas at all, so I can see some of the seams on this backpack getting easily stressed when you are carrying especially heavy loads. The zippers and connectors are of about average quality. One detail that caught my eye was one of the larger zippers on the inside of the pack. It's actually stitched in backwards, which makes one compartment impossible to zip up, unless you were zipping it from the inside of the backpack! We all have one of those days, I guess. Someone definitely was asleep at the wheel in quality control this particular day.

The materials and construction are 100% Made in China. This definitely accounts for it's bargain price, but also explains some of the corners that were cut. This backpack is definitely adequate for casual use, but it certainly isn't something that you would want to use while climbing Mt. Everest or going on a professional expedition. For most of us though, this model will definitely do the job it was intended for and looks great while doing it.

reviews.title: Great vest, not that great a bottle
reviews.text:
I have a Camelback hydration pack that I love, but in the desert sun, it makes me a bit hot. I wanted a pack that covered less of my body, but still carried a nice 2L bottle to provide plenty of water for longer hikes, strolls or bike rides.

This pack is great. The lime green color is a bit "louder" than I would prefer, but it covers less of my torso, so I don't get overheated as easily. It’s made of a strong nylon material that seems to be waterproof. There are several highly reflective stripes that make you visible in low light.

The pouch for the hydration pack zips open nice and wide, so it's easier to get the bottle in and out. You thread the hose from the back to the front through the section where the back attaches to the strap, which is also easier to manage. There's room for a cell phone, sunglasses case and other small items in the pocket in front of the pouch in the back. However, if you have ice water in the pouch, they may get damp when condensation collects around the bag. There’s also the inconvenience of having to take the vest off or have someone get your stuff out for you that way. The crisscross cord in the back may allow you to carry a hiking pole, jacket or something else outside the pack.

I do miss having the clip for the mouthpiece I had on my Camelback vest. With this one, you have to reach down and grab the hose dangling at your side. There are clips on the front to allow you to hang a key chain or carabiners. There are adjustable straps to fit it to your body shape at the chest, from the bottom of the vest front to the back, and from the back around the waist.

The bottle is not that great. The opening is small, and it doesn’t have the handle to help you grasp and hold it open to fill it like my Camelback. I miss the quick-release valve at the bottom, too. For this one, you have to screw in the hose. The mouthpiece is fairly easy to use: You remove the white cap and pull the silicone mouthpiece up to open the valve. My Camelback bottle has a mouthpiece that you just bite down on to open the valve. Another issue is that the plastic seems a bit thin and may burst or spring a leak easier than my heavy-duty Camelback. One advantage this has over the other is the two openings at the top that allow you to hang the bag to air out.

If you don’t need a lot of stuff with you and want to stay cool during a hike, this vest may work for you. Nevertheless, I can’t really recommend the water bottle. You’d be better off getting a quality hydration bottle from another company. The price of about $25 seems fair. Yet, I think it would be better if these folks offered the vest by itself for about $15, and then you could buy a different 2L bottle.

reviews.title: Worth Every Penny
reviews.text:
I am a long term Maxpedition customer. I carried the Falcon II every day for nearly four years, packed to the gills. I needed to increase in size over the Falcon II and settled on the Falcon III since I was already comfortable with the design. It gives me enough additional capacity that it's not over-stuffed with my EDC gear. I prefer the design of the new zippers. I did like the separate zip up hydration bladder pocket of the Falcon II for CCW. But the same thing can be accomplished with the middle compartment on this pack. One addition I really like is the chest strap that keeps the shoulder straps in place. This pack is expensive, but it's worth every penny. I can highly recommend this for every day carry if you need a pack that will hold up over time. Maxpedition got it right again!

Update: January 29, 2107 - Still a great pack, no defects and still looks good. I will try to post an update again next year.

reviews.title: Sturdy bag, worth the investment
reviews.text:
I've owned the Falcon III for only two days, and I've had it on just one hike, and so far, I am VERY happy with the purchase. I ordered Khaki, which in the Amazon product listing, Khaki looks more like a desert sand color throughout, and the straps are the same color as the canvas. HOWEVER, what actually showed up is two-tone that leans more toward a green, and seems more like a different color Maxpedition offers, despite the label correctly saying Khaki. (I had earlier ordered the Falcon II in Khaki, and same thing, what showed up was very olive-like with tan straps.) I returned the Falcon II partly because of the wrong color, but also because I felt it was just too small for an adult, though it would be good for a kid or tween.

All of that said, I do like the Falcon III in whatever color they sent to me. Ha! Keep reading for actual review stuff...

STURDY
This is legit fabric. You can take it out of the box, open it up, and it will stand up on the floor all by itself! It's that rigid. The seams and sewing all seem very well done. The Molle feels really strong. The straps and buckles don't feet cheap. I think some people will probably say, "oh, the fabric is so hard and rough, I am sending this back." But the way I see it, you want something heavy duty that will take whatever you throw at it. I seriously can't imagine using this thing so much that it wears a hole in the fabric. That seems impossible. I think you could fill this up and drag it on the dirt behind a truck, and... no problems.

SIZE
Okay, I am a 6-foot big dude and probably pushing 285 lb. The pack is easy to put on and easy to take off. I wasn't squirming or stretching or contorting myself to get it on or off. The overall size is great. During my hike today, I never felt like it was this tiny thing on my back... and I never felt like it was some ginormous camp-in-the-woods-for-a-month obnoxious pack. It just seemed perfect in size. The bottom of the pack hung down to just above my butt. And again, I was super glad I returned the Falcon II so that I could have the larger Falcon III. I could easily walk, hike, bike or travel with the Falcon III. It would be a great bag to fill up with essentials and get on an airplane without checking larger bags.

POCKETS & STORAGE
The main large pocket is big and I could very easily put my laptop computer in here. The large pocket includes a pouch where you can drop in your water bladder, and there are two covered holes (one on either size) for your water hose to come out. In that water pocket, if you didn't want to put water in there, it's big enough for a small chromebook, or a book or notepad. Also in the main pocket, there is a netted pocket that is not zippered. I put two books in there. There's plenty of space left for a jacket or blanket some extra small clothes, etc.
The middle-sized pocket is just as deep as the big main pocket. This middle area has no organization. I used this space for my small medical kit and a very large 1.5 liter water bottle. And there was quite a bit of empty space left for more stuff.
The outside pocket on top is not very deep and has no organization inside. It's big enough for a sandwich and a granola bar or two, but not much else. On my hike today I had a bag of peanuts, three granola bars and my sunglasses.
The outside pocket on the bottom is a much larger external space and it has more organization for pens, knife, flashlight, and a hanger for keys. There's also a rear pouch inside. There was some extra space, but I would not put anything in there that is fragile (like a phone) since your knife and keys, could scratch it.
My only complaint here is that I am jealous of other bags that have more organization in the main compartments. If I was the designer, I guess I would have added a zipper to at least one of the compartments in the primary space.... and for sure I would add another pouch (or two) in the secondary space. But maybe Maxpedition's M.O. is that they want customers to buy more pouches to store stuff internally, and externally via molle.

BUCKLES & STRAPS
The main shoulder straps are padded and comfortable. They have no storage on them, though there are D-rings and molle so you can add pouches, etc. The padding on the shoulder straps is the same material as what's on the main back pad.
The sternum buckle is plenty long to fit me (again, I am a big guy). I used it during my hike just to keep the shoulder straps in place. I never hiked without it connected, so I can't say how the whole thing hangs without the sternum strap connected.
The waist strap just hangs and cannot be stored or put away. That's kinda weird. Anyway, I hiked without putting it around me. I just buckled the two sides together and let it hang. That was never uncomfortable and really I never felt it or thought about it.
The compression straps all around are good and also don't get in the way. You can compress two straps from back to front. And you can connect one compression strap from top to bottom. I think they did a good job with this.

AIR FLOW & MAIN PADDING
I don't know what you call the main pad that actual touches your back, but that whole area is a black net finish on top of the padding (same as the shoulder straps). If anything on this bag is going to ever tear, it's that black netting. But it felt perfectly soft and comfortable on my back during my hike today. It was only about 74 degrees, so not hot enough to sweat my butt off. So I can't tell about the air flow. But so far it seems fine. My back certainly never felt wet.

WHAT ELSE?
I guess that's about all I can say. I am a pretty frugal guy and it took some convincing to make myself spend $150 on a backpack. But I have lived long enough to know that it's probably a good investment and will likely be the last backpack I have to buy. It's certainly not going to fall apart like the $30 bag I bought in 2017 (multiple ripping problems and straps disintegrating!) So would I rather buy a new $30 backpack every few years, or just spend $150 now on a quality back that I can get used to and have for a decade or more?

reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:670390d5f4bbbcd1c8a0c687f3650946]] Let me start by saying that I am a person that does a lot of research before buying an item. I don't spend on a whim. It may take me weeks or a month before making that buying commitment. I look for something that has all the features I need.
I was looking to replace my air Jordan sling that I've had for at least 15 years , maybe longer. First choice was another air Jordan but I could not get the same style..so I started hunting.
This brand seemed to fit my needs. Had many of the same feature as my old backpack..and this has a bottle holder which my old one did not have. BONUS :) So I waited till prime day and got this for 10dollars cheaper . Oh ,and the reviews were decent .
Well it arrived today and I couldn't be more disappointed. This is really small for my needs. Measurements on this are embellished. Reviews said this was great for a day trip or hike but honestly if you just wear a Tshirt and shorts you would be ok. I wanted to fit work clothes and my lunch in this bag but that isn't happening.
There are many pockets but let's be honest, you can only fit so much inside this bag. Extra pockets don't give you more space, they provide just separation.
We shall see how the durability of this is. No way it will give me 15 years as I'm pretty rough on my bag as it goes everywhere I go. It's hard letting go of a good pair of shoes or a bag or any fashion you have had for many years cause it's hard to replace something so durable. I'm sure many have had that experience.
Overall this is just to small for my needs as you can see in the picture. The measurements are a stretch. Durability we will see and I will update.
1 WEEK later......no issues with the bag. I have been gentle as far as overstuffing it. The size issue is muy inconvenient. Many issues on that topic but just one......I work outdoors and head to work with a hoodie cause its chilly in the a.m. the hoodie wont fit in the bag when the weather warms and i only have a shirt, lunchbag, phone/charger, misc stuff already in it.. Reading the comments , This makes me curious what kind of day trip people are taking in order to use this bag in that fashion..

reviews.title: Good for show
reviews.text:
I'm only keeping it because I really like the size, I haven't tested it's water resistance and I hate returning things.
This pack is cool until you get up close. Mine arrived with frilled strap ends and minor damage to the back padding. See my pictures.
The molle system is not standard. I use OneTigris products. You'll get 1 strap in but the next loop will be too narrow.
The sewing is uneven so if you look closely you'll see nothing is stitched square. Like the front pouches.
The sternum strap is designed horribly because if you tighten it will will scrunch up the shoulder strap.
The waist strap isn't useful either, since the belt cannot be locked into a setting. If you pull it will just loosen right up.
The shoulder straps twist as you put it on and they are rough so you can't wear it over your bare skin, like when you want to go down to a tank top layer.
I gave it 3 stars because if you don't have plans to modify it for extra uses it's good. It looks and feels sturdy and it fits just enough for the day in an organized way. The straps I have a problem with I will remove. I'll use it until it wears and shop for a better one.

If you've ever had to stow your gear with other travelers, you'd appreciate having a brightly colored bag like this each time you went to retrieve it. If you prefer a more subdued color, this bag also comes in blue and black options. The main compartment of this daypack is also roomy and comes with a laptop pocket with decent padding at the back. The only things I would change about this bag would be by adding some more padded reinforcement at the bottom, and include a rain cover that would protect the open top compartment above the brand logo. All the same, I can still get a great deal of use out of this bag as a lightweight daypack or overnight bag.

On the front-bottom of the pack is another small pocket- however these items will rest on the bottom of the main compartment when the pack in on the ground, so any fragile items in here may not hold up well. The side straps are useful-ish, with the option to cinch them down for the pack to fit better, or they offer a small bit of room for stuffing items. reviews.title: Great Little Hydration Pack
reviews.text: I bought this for short (~3 hr) summer hikes in the mid-Atlantic region, where I need a lot of water.  The 2L hydration pack was perfect for that.  The bladder works well, the connector to the hose is solid.  The only "trick" was that I have to thread the hose through all of the holders on the strap and into the bag itself before connecting it to the bladder, since the mouthpiece is too large to thread though.  The bladder sits in an insulated section of the pack, so it holds the cool temperature pretty well, even better if you dump some ice in before you leave home.  What I really like is how much other stuff fits in the pack:  tissues, hand sanitizer, headband, my huge wallet, and a hat (and I don't even stuff it full).  The laces on the outside of the pack would even accommodate a light jacket.  There are two hip pockets, neither of which is large enough for my iPhone 8 plus without having to really work it in there, but it great for chapstick and my car keys (there is no clip inside for keys, as I have in other packets, but one of the hip band pockets works just fine for this)!  This is an ideal alternative to my large Osprey pack when I need to take a lot of water with me on a hike and I don't want to wear a large pack.  The pack also comes with a little flexible cleaner for the hose and with an extra gasket for the hose-bladder connection.  Great buy!

reviews.title: Bladder failed at a critical moment
reviews.text: I purchased this hydration backpack with the 3L water bladder in mid April, in preparation for a long US roadtrip with several visits to national and state parks. With lots of hiking in hot weather, I needed a reliable hydration source. Unfortunately this product wasn’t it. I tested the bladder system at home, and it seemed OK. However, the bladder didn’t survive its first real world test. In Canyonlands, Utah, with 100+ degree weather, two things happened: (1) the suction end got punctured within minutes. It still worked and didn’t leak, so I kept on using it throughout the day. (2) At the end of the day, back at the hotel, when I tried to refill the bladder I couldn’t get the bladder seal off. The hard plastic handle/seal doesn’t budge at all, and it almost seems as if it has fused closed (I don’t think that’s possible, but the reality is I can’t slide it at all, and yes, I am doing it in the right direction.) Bottom line: I am at the beginning of a series of hikes, left without this key component of my hydration system (fortunately I have backups, though I’ll miss having a hydration backpack/water bladder, and it’s beyond the return window, so I’m out of money as well. I know that the vast majority of the reviews are positive (that’s why I bought this item!), but based on my experience I cannot recommend this product. One star from me.

reviews.title: Great Gopack For Kids!
reviews.text:
This shoulder backpack has a good size for bigger kids. My daughter is 9 years old, and it’s right on. She is keeping travel essentials in it, having it ready for trips. It is basically a kids version of a gopack, with underwear, extra socks, cereal bars, leggings, facemasks (against air pollution and smoke in the event of wildfires, not to go to the store), water bottle, walkie talkie, gotenna and some other tricks. It doesn't replace the bigger version, that is packed to evacuate, or the duffle bag in the car, but in case we are stranded, there is enough to stay a day or two. Be prepared, be ready.
The quality is good. Even the zippers seem to be better than from what I experienced with cheaper bags in the past. The velcro is strong, and the sling has extra loops, which is great. Many sling-bags leave the sling space unused or just add an extra zipper.
I am giving this product five stars. On a budget this is a good bag. Clearly not as good as a product that is specifically designed to take it into the field, but my guess is that it can withstand a kid for about a year. More if not used daily. Neat: The hidden zipper at the bottom!

reviews.title: Futuristic looking, easy to use.
reviews.text:
This is a really cool looking coffee maker. Very futuristic, especially with the red light while brewing.
It's a little bit larger than my ninja coffee bar. Slightly taller and slightly wider. I ordered this to replace the Ninja because the Ninja keeps giving me the five beeps of death and will not brew or clean anymore. This one is a totally different setup and doesn't have all the bells and whistles, but makes a solid cup of coffee.
The water goes in the back compartment, filter and coffee grounds in the front. Very simple instructions, easy to understand, presented well.
The options are bold or normal brew coffee, timed coffee making, keep warm, and makes up to 12 cups.
The fact that the coffee carafe and be accessed within a 180° range is a great and helpful feature.
It does not specifically say it will brew a single cup, but since I drink a 20 oz mug of coffee every morning and not a tiny cup, that is not an issue. It handled the 20 oz perfectly fine.
I am really pleased with this coffee maker, I recommend it.
EDIT: After using this for a couple weeks, I've got a couple more observations. Unless I'm missing something, you have to add water each time for the exact amount of coffee you want - I see no setting for serving size options. I generally put the amount of water I want in the mug that I want to use and pour it into the water compartment. Would be nice to fill the water and just hit a size button.
Also, there is a lot of condensation at the top of the grounds compartment, but i just tap the lid before I open it and that takes off most of the condensation.
I removed a star because of the inability to choose brew size.

reviews.title: Failed on first use - Updated
reviews.text:
First use the unit heated too temp of 99c shut off okay great. welll not great lifted it up and hot water was leaking out the bottom into my cup holder. Now has steam in the window and controls don’t work. I’m pretty certain the relief valve failed to open. It’s possible I just got a bad one. Trying another will update:

Update:
Purchased another unit and this one seems fine However I Removed the check ball out of the silicone seal in the cap. I’m very certain this is what caused my first failure with not venting pressure during the unit coming to a boil consequently making the lower body seals start leaking. It’s actually safer with it removed abit of steam comes out when it nears boil but that’s better than opening a pressurized vessel as many have encountered. With the check ball removed mine goes to 99c shuts off and I can open it immediately with no boil flare up. I’ve tested it about two dozen times and currently traveling the east coast so far it’s not failed. Keep in mind if your heating to a boil and removed your pressure check ball it will steam some out the hole on the cap it’s not much you may not even notice it but be aware. I fill mine to the max fill line and it has never spit water out the hole. Anyway be careful of any steam!

I’m giving 4 stars as of now due to the pressure relief flaw

But the main advantage is being able to let each person make coffee on their own schedule, so it’s always fresh.  We tried using a Keurig with fresh ground coffee and it was so weak we hated it. reviews.title: Get off the fence!
reviews.text:
Edit: February 13, 2022

I knocked 3 stars off my original rating, it doesn't heat the water properly. If I don't use hot water, I'll get lukewarm coffee. It's a shame because otherwise this thing is amazing. Blerg.

This is my second grind and brew coffee machine. My first, the Viatne Mini Grind & Brew, which for all ts fickleness served me well for 2+ years. It too had a good amount of critical ratings but I stuck with it and was rewarded with freshly ground & brewed coffee every morning and have zero regrets.

The Power XL Grind & Go is an improvement in almost every area. It has less parts, is more efficient and is not as fickle as the Viante.

It takes about 6 minutes for the grind & brew cycle to complete and yes it makes noise (as does anything grinding up stuff!). It does not have a hot plate so you'll want to time it so that you're ready to drink your deliciousness when its done brewing.

The Viante had a hot plate and to be honest I never really let my coffee sit for very long seeing as how it was only a single cup. I mean, it's not like you need to keep an entire pot of coffee warm.

Anyway, you must make sure the notches are properly aligned after you load the beans in the grinder but otherwise, I've found it pretty much idiot proof.

This is a cool little machine which has taken the concept of the single serve grind & brew coffee maker and improved on it immensely in my opinion. No, it has not been perfected quite yet but it's getting there!

Gabi Master A – June 2021

I am now a HUGE fan of this device. Please read through all of my updates as they will show how I have evolved my use of the Gabi Master A.

Note: The Gabi distribution holes WILL clog. They’re tiny and any sediment, etc. may clog. So always test it by pouring some water into it without the paper filter or coffee to make sure water is passing through each hole. If not, try blowing it out or wiping the holes with a sponge. Just be sure you have correct flow before making your coffee each morning. It just takes a minute.

Original Comment - Gabi Master A.
One thing. The first time you assemble you’re gonna be nervous about that push hard to fit, the water bottle and water spout, cause there aren’t notches to fit, it’s a compression fit. So just push it down. I was afraid of breaking it the first time but I took a chance and it worked.
Kalita 155 which I didn’t have, so I trimmed a 185.
I’ll report on coffee quality after playing with it for a week.

Update 1 - This is kind of interesting. Noting a lukewarm cup of coffee, I poured 210 F boiling water through the unit with no coffee but with the paper filter. The water temp in the carafe measured 145 F.

Update 2 - Moving into the next brew and experiments. You know? I’m beginning to think that the Rao Swirl is preferable for coffee saturation to this device (re:temperature drop)...

Update 3 - Something is not right. I'm thinking the Gabi is more of a “fun gadget”. Check this out. Normally with the Rao Swirl, we’d see a nice even bed of coffee. Look at the results of the Gabi. 36 grams, 576 ml. Water temp after extraction. 150 F. Flavorwise, thinner but tasty.

Update 4 - 15 g at 160 ml. Uneven and incomplete extraction. As noted by some, their recommendation for ratio is different than SCAA standards, per their brochure so keep this in mind.

Update 5 - You know, as I settle in with really evaluating today’s extraction, it is flavorful. It makes me want to keep working with this device. Maybe it is irrelevant if the coffee bed doesn’t look like it normally would.

Update 6 - I’m now adding a swirl (aka the Rao Swirl) after the first pour that they recommend to soak the beans. I’ve now tried several of the recommended coffee and water ratios they recommend in the booklet that comes with the device. I’m starting to like some of the flavor profiles. But not all. I think I may be turning into a fan for this gadget. Time will tell. Gonna take a break and then come back with a four way test with standard Kalita and two grind sizes and then the same grind sizes with the Gabi Master A. For a side by side comparison. Will update later.

Update 7 - I’m still torn on whether to recommend or not. I did a serious, controlled experiment with 12 g coffee and 200 ml. I did two different grind settings on my Baratza (extreme settings of 10 and 24 to really push the envelope as it were) and made coffee with a standard Kalita 185. Then I did the same grinds with the Gabi. Whereas with only my Kalita, the coffee was acceptable with both grinds, slight differences in acidity but not significant (more bitterness with the finer grind), the fine grind was not good with the Gabi. There was a paper-y taste that I can't explain. Because I had rinsed the filters in all cases. (Note: if you are starting out, do a water taste test. Run some water through a Kalita filter, about 100 ml, and pour 100 ml straight from your kettle. Cool and taste both. If you can't tell the difference, rinsing you paper filter probably isn't necessary before brewing...having said that I always rinse my filter cause I've always done that). Only the coarser grind was flavorful and actually nice. Thus, my recommendation is to buy the Gabi if you want to add a coolness factor to your morning brew and don’t mind working really hard to find the sweet spot. Otherwise, just stick with your standard Kalita pour over method and save $35.

Update 8 – Oh heck, just buy it and have fun with it.

Update 9 - That paper taste. So, I’m having coffee with a friend and his first question is “is there a significant temperature drop in the device because water temper contributes to the paper taste”. The aha moment. This is what is happening. So it is imperative that you rinse the Kalita filter with boiling hot water after putting it in the basket in order to warm up the plastic a little and remove the paper taste.

Update 10 - one final test. I pulled out my Kalita and added 18 grams of coffee to it. I set up my scale and 3 glasses. Using my scale to keep track, I did three pours of 100 ml each. The first 100 would be the strongest of course and the third would be the weakest and possibly the most sour. Note: I did not zero out the scale for the second and third pours. I tasted all three. I then did exactly the same but with the Gabi.

I let them cool. And tasted and compared.

There was a more “paper” taste to the third cup of the Gabi than with the Kalita. But it was also thinner but less sour. The first cup of the Gabi was more intense than the Kalita, more syrupy, and more coffee components were extracted, almost like what one would see with a phin extraction. Combing cups one and two of the Gabi resulted in a stronger more intense coffee. I didn’t use the third cup in both cases. I think I may have liked the less intense Kalita extraction. But with this last experiment, I am reverting back, adding a star and giving the Gabi a recommendation. Once more.

Update 11 - As of June 2021, I am now a fan, and recommend the Gabi without hesitation. Into a double wall Kalita carafe, I set up the Gabi with the white Kalita 155 filter paper that I pre-rinsed just enough so that any paper powder was rinsed out but the ridges weren't collapsed. Do your rinsing in the Gabi as the walls will keep the Kalita filter rigid during rinsing. I then grind 24 grams of coffee with my Baratza Virtuoso Plus on a #16 setting (note: when I get a new bag of coffee, I always do three tests of 12g coffee to 200 ml water at grind settings of 10, 16, and 22. I do these with a Kalita 185 and no Gabi. I then taste each extraction and decide which grind produced the tastiest coffee). I pour 400 ml (that's the SCAA 16:1 ratio) of water in 3 pours. And as I've noted, I am well pleased with the results. Additional note: I'd recommend also buying the Gabi Master B. I use that with a Kalita 185 and 36 grams of coffee to 600 ml water.

reviews.title: A Turkish man told me that only copper should be used in a cezve...
reviews.text:
... So I purchased this one. It says it is "hand hammered," which looks to be kinda-true. It looks like the factory took some machine-made pots, then someone took a hammer to it to make it look hammered. It's amazing. The cezve itself looks stout enough that if not used as a coffee maker, it could probably work as a bludgeoning device. Honestly, I really don't care, I wanted a one-cup cezve for my coffee explorations and the Turk I work with said only use a copper cezve.

I got some Kurukahveci Mehmet Efendi and Cafe Najar with cardamom pre-ground, because my grinder can't made coffee fine enough for use in a cezve. Sure, it can grind it down to a consistency for use in an espresso machine, but not fine enough for use in a cezve. Oh well. Anywho, I put the coffee in, mixed in some warm water, put it over medium flame and within seven minutes I got coffee. Overall, the cezve works as a cezve.

The good: It is beautiful. The touch screen controls are easy to use and easy to clean. It is a lovely coffee maker. It works fine--much the same as cheaper coffee makers, in my opinion.

Why the poor rating? After just a month or two of normal once per day use, the paint on the burner started coming off. It's worse now. Very unsightly. reviews.title: Simple Drip Coffee Brewing
reviews.text: This makes good coffee. The instructions call for a kitchen scale and a timer, though, which I do not have. I filled the thermos part with water to measure, and placed that amount of water in the pot to heat. You are supposed to weigh each amount of water that you pour over the coffee grounds, swirl the water in a certain manner, and time how long they drain. I was not this precise, and the coffee came out very delicious. The glass carafe assembly is still hot after pouring the first cup, so one must carefully remove in order to place the lid on the thermos. I was concerned that I would have to reattach the carafe for subsequent cups, but it is just as easy to pour from the lower thermos part. It is very nice to have hot coffee for later, and this brewing process does make very good coffee.

reviews.title: MY FIRST EXPRESSO MACHINE!  JUST PERFECT!
reviews.text:
This is my very first Expresso Machine and I am uber-excited! I have wanted one of these coffee makers for years, but space was always an issue. This slim, low-profile maker is the solution to my problem, and it could not have come at a better time.

My husband completed the plans for the renovation of my studio. To my surprise, he included a space for a coffee bar. Imagine my surprise when this beauty became available in the Vine Program. The size was exactly what I wanted and it seemed less intimidating than other Expresso Machines I had researched.

I am currently waiting for the delivery of my cartridges. Being a novice, I was not aware that the cartridges are not included. This is noted in the description, but in my excitement, I must have overlooked it!

The Expresso Machine is low-profile with a small footprint. The 37oz water tank is 2-3 oz larger than comparable machines! The price falls in the middle of similar machines! The instruction manual is detailed and easy to understand.

Since we are about three weeks away from the completion of my studio renovations, and because I have no cartridges, I cannot comment on how well the machine operates! It has received very positive reviews and I expect that my experience will be no different. If it is, I will update this review.

The Expresso Machine is made of good quality materials. It is fully featured and easy to operate. This machine is ideal for small spaces.

reviews.title: It's beautiful, well made, iconic, and bad at coffee making
reviews.text:
So well made.
So stylish.
Great packaging.
Great materials.
It's perfect.
Except it's much much worse as a moka pot, than the Bialetti Venus that costs about 1/4.

At the end of the day, the latching mechanism doesn't work as well as a screw top on the default mocha pots. It's both harder to use, and doesn't seal nearly as well. I spent a week trying to get this to produce coffee without spitting boiling water. In the end, I failed, gave up, and returned it.

Yeah, there are tricks, hacks, techniques....but. Why? At it's best it'll match the Venus. At worst it costs more, is more temperamental, and makes worse coffee.

Great art piece.
Not a great coffee making device.

reviews.title: This is the ultimate Moka pot
reviews.text:
I live within walking distance from three roasters. I can get amazing expresso whenever I want. But, I like to roast unique beans and brew at home. Sometimes I use an AeroPress. But, most of the time I use the Alessi. It is NOT an Espresso maker. It is its own kinda animal. I've own several Moka pots over the years and the Richard Sapper design takes it to a new level. The quick release handle is literally a snap to clean.

To brew I preheat filtered water before filling the bottom reservoir. Main difference with an espresso machine is to back off from compressing the grounds in the porto filter. The main action is more convection than pressure. So, the water needs room to flow. You'll know you have the right grind, compactness, and heat, is when it only starts to sputter after it is nearly full. If it sputters too soon, then it means that the water is having a hard time making its way through the grounds. Turn up the heat too high, and the first part of the extraction will over cook. After a few tries, it will become second nature. And what you'll have is the perfect Moka cup.
